# Google Business Profile Automation: The Complete Guide for Local Businesses

D

Dammy

Aug 13, 2026 · 21 min read

[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdmly.io%2Fgoogle-business-profile-automation-guide%2F)

![Google Business Profile Automation: The Complete Guide for Local Businesses](https://dmly.io/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Google-Business-Profile-Automation.png)

Your Google Business Profile may be one of the first things people see when they search for your business. But keeping it active means checking reviews, replying to customers, updating information, and remembering to ask happy customers for feedback.

For a busy local business, those little tasks pile up fast.

But with Google Business Profile automation, you can take much of that repetitive work off your plate. You can automatically request reviews after customer visits, keep track of new feedback, manage your profile, and use AI to help with responses.

In this guide, we’ll look at what you can automate, what you should still handle personally, and how to build a system that keeps your Google presence working even when you’re busy elsewhere.

## **What Is Google Business Profile Automation?**

Google Business Profile automation, also known as GBP automation, is the use of software and automated workflows to handle repetitive tasks involved in managing your business presence on Google.

Instead of remembering to check your profile and perform every action manually, you can set up certain tasks to happen automatically when something triggers them.

Take reviews as an example. Normally, your receptionist might finish an appointment, remember to message the customer later, find your [Google review link](https://dmly.io/google-review-link/), and send it manually. With automation, completing the appointment can trigger the review request for you.

The same idea can apply to other parts of profile and reputation management. Depending on the software you use, you can:

*   Send automated Google review requests after customer visits
*   Monitor new reviews without constantly checking Google
*   Get notified when customers leave feedback
*   Draft review responses with AI
*   Manage business information and opening hours
*   Publish and manage Google Business Profile posts
*   Manage several business locations from one place

The important word here is **automation**. You’re deciding beforehand what should happen when a particular event occurs.

For example:

**Appointment completed → wait 2 hours → send customer a WhatsApp review request → customer opens your Google review link → new review appears → team is notified → AI helps draft the response**

## **What Parts of a Google Business Profile Can You Automate?**

**Start with the shape of it, because the boundary is sharper than most articles on this subject admit.** A connected Google Business Profile gives you five tabs and no more: Performance, Reviews, Request reviews, Posts and Business info. If a job is not one of those five, it is still a job you do on Google.

![A filing drawer with five labelled tabs and two panels beside it. The tabs are the five Reputation tabs: Posts, Business info and Performance marked in green as this page's subject, and Reviews and Request reviews marked in amber and labelled as the review guide's. The first panel separates what can be edited here, phone, website, description and opening hours, from what is read-only, business name, category and address. The second panel, in red, lists three things that are not in the drawer at all: questions and answers on your listing, messaging of any kind, and replying twice to the same review. A footer warns that every Reputation tab shows made-up sample data until a profile is connected.](https://dmly.io/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/what-a-connected-google-business-profile-actually-covers.png)

**Figure 1.** Five tabs, two of which are the review guide’s subject. The panel on the right is the part worth reading twice.

Three absences are worth stating plainly, because assuming any of them costs you a morning.

**Questions and answers on your listing are not managed here.** The Q&A section that appears under a Google listing is not one of the five tabs, so answering a question a customer has posted is something you do on Google. It is worth doing: a good Q&A section answers the queries that would otherwise become phone calls. It is just not a thing you can automate from outside.

**It is not a messaging channel.** No chats, no broadcasts, no bot. A review is the only conversation Google gives you here, and the customer cannot reply to your reply. If you want to actually talk to the people leaving reviews, that happens on [a channel that carries messages](https://dmly.io/whatsapp-broadcasts-for-businesses-guide/).

**Photos reach your listing through a post, not through a photo manager.** You can attach one to an update, an offer or an event. There is no gallery to curate from here, so the photos on your listing stay Google’s business.

### **The numbers you see before you connect are not yours**

Worth knowing on day one. Every Reputation tab works before a profile is attached, and what it shows is **sample data**: made-up reviews, made-up names, made-up numbers, with a badge and a prompt saying so. It is there to show you the shape of the thing. It is not hard to mistake for your own listing on a Monday morning, and people do.

Quite a bit of the day-to-day work around your Google Business Profile can be automated or managed through one central system. The trick is knowing which tasks are repetitive enough to hand over and which ones still deserve your attention.

Here are some of the most useful areas to consider.

This is probably the biggest opportunity for local businesses.

**Picture this:** You want a traditional Indian meal for your dinner today and you search online for local restaurants that serve the best Indian cuisine. While searching you find two options. One has a vibrant **Google Business Profile** filled with **delicious food photos and glowing reviews**. The other one has no Google profile or any recent information. 

Now I have a question: Which restaurant are you more likely to visit?

It’s clear: Anyone would choose a restaurant that has an updated and organized  **Google My Business Profile(GMB).** Now imagine keeping your profile feed fresh automatically from WordPress without even thinking about it twice. 

That’s what I’ll cover today! In this blog, I’ll be sharing how to auto-post to Google My Business from WordPress automatically using an easy-to-use social media automation tool [Bit Social](https://wordpress.org/plugins/bit-social/). And here’s the cherry on top: I’ll also be showing you how to schedule your Google Business Profile posts in advance so that your business stays at the top of local search results. Also lastly I’ll be focusing on the importance of Google Business Profile for any business. So stay tuned.

After forming the connection between Bit Social and Google Business Profile, I’ll be showing you multiple ways of posting from your WordPress dashboard.

It’s as simple as that!

To get started with the WP Auto Post feature, just follow these easy steps, and you’ll be all set to automate your posting journey.

**Step 1:** Open Bit Social dashboard > Connect account > Move to the “**WP AutoPost**” feature. 

1.  Enable the “**Share posts automatically**” option, to share the post on all active social accounts automatically.
2.  Enable the “**Enable auto post log**” option, this allows all your shared posts to be recorded in the log section, where you can review them.
3.  Select the “**Share post type**” whether it’s a post, page, product, or media.
4.  Set “**Share post delay**”, this tells when your posts will be shared after publishing on WordPress.

**Step 2:** From the right side select “[**Templates**](https://bit-social.com/documentation/templates/)” > Customize your message here using “**Smart Tags**”

**Step 3:** Select the **Posting type** and **Button type**

**Step 4:** Publish a content on WordPress 

**Step 5:** Check “**Logs**” whether it is published or not. 

Congratulations! Your content has successfully been published on Google Business Profile.

This powerful n8n workflow automatically generates and publishes Google Business Profile (GMB) posts using topics listed in a Google Sheet.  
It uses **OpenAI** to write SEO-optimized post descriptions and generate **AI images** based on the topic — then posts them directly to your **GMB profile** and marks them as published in the sheet.

## 🎯 Use Case

Perfect for:

*   Digital marketers managing local SEO
*   Agencies automating content for clients
*   Businesses regularly posting to GMB
*   Teams managing editorial calendars via Google Sheets

## ⚙️ Workflow Overview

| 🧩 Node | 🔧 Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| 🕘 **Schedule Trigger** | Runs daily at 9AM (configurable) |
| 📄 **Get Unpublished Row** | Reads a row from Google Sheet where Status is not marked "Published" |
| ✍️ **Generate Post Text** | Uses OpenAI (GPT-4) to write a compelling, local-business optimized post |
| 🖼 **Generate Post Image** | Uses DALL·E or similar to create an image matching the topic |
| 📬 **Post to GMB** | Publishes the generated content to your Google Business Profile |
| ✅ **Update Sheet** | Marks the status as "Published" in the Google Sheet |

## 📄 Google Sheet Format

| Column Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Topic | The subject or idea for the GMB post |
| Status | Should be blank or "Unpublished" to trigger the flow |
| Date | (Optional) Posting schedule or note |
| Notes | (Optional) Internal info — not used in the automation |

## 🔐 Google My Business API Setup

### 1\. Google Cloud Configuration

*   Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/)
*   Enable the **Google My Business API**
*   Create **OAuth2 Client ID** and **Client Secret**
*   Add this required scope:

### 2\. Request for GMB Quota

*   You need to request for GMB (Google Business Profile) API Quota from here, beacuse by deafult it sets to zero: [https://support.google.com/business/contact/api\_default](https://support.google.com/business/contact/api_default)

### 3\. n8n Credential Setup

*   In n8n, go to **Credentials > Google OAuth2**
*   Use your **Client ID** and **Client Secret**
*   Use this credential in GMB-related nodes

## 🧠 OpenAI Prompt Customization

Modify the prompt in the OpenAI node to match your brand’s voice:

### Example Prompt

`Write a short, engaging Google Business Post about: "{{ $json.topic }}". Make it suitable for a local audience and include a subtle call to action.`

## 🧪 Optional Enhancements

*   Add **If** node to delay publishing on certain days
*   Use **Slack or Email** notifications to alert before/after posting
*   Use **Multiple Businesses** by adding a Router or Switch node per GMB account

## ✅ Benefits

*   🔁 Fully automated GMB posting
*   ✍️ SEO-optimized, AI-written content
*   🖼 Matching images for visual engagement
*   📊 Maintains a content log via Google Sheets

# Create & manage posts on your Business Profile

You can post updates on your Business Profile to share announcements, offers, updates, and event details directly with your customers on Search and Maps. When customers find your latest business updates on your Business Profile, it helps them decide to visit your business.

Post on your Business Profile to:

*   Share up-to-date info and improve your customer experience.
*   Promote your sales, specials, events, news, and offers.
*   Connect with your customers through posts with photos and videos.

Understand where customers can find your posts

Posts can show text, photos, or videos, and customers can find them in:

*   The “Updates” or “Overview” tabs of the Business Profile on mobile on Search and Maps.
*   The “From the owner” section of the Business Profile on your computer on Search and Maps.
*   Featured posts that are added directly to your Business Profile on mobile.

Posts about events, deals, or specials may automatically show on your Business Profile on mobile. These featured posts are from your social media channels, like Facebook and Instagram, or from posts you've created on your Business Profile.

**Tips:**

*   This feature is currently available in English for single-location food and drink businesses in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.
*   When featured posts are available, customers find them in place of reviews on your Business Profile on mobile. They can still access reviews when they tap your business's star rating or check the "Reviews" tab.

Understand the different types of posts

**Important:** Posts that include a phone number in the post description might get rejected if they cannot be verified as being connected to the business on which they are posted. To add additional phone numbers to your profile, [learn more about edits to your Business Profile](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617#phone).

You can create and customize these types of posts:

*   **Updates:** Share info about your business.
    *   You can add a description, photo, video, and an action button with a link. The button should direct customers to a website where they can complete the action, like make a booking, order online, or learn more.
*   **Offers:** Provide promotional sales or offers from your business.
    *   It requires a title, dates, and time. This automatically includes a "View Offer" button on the post. You can also include a description, photo, video, coupon code, link, and terms and conditions. [Learn more about managing offers on your Business Profile](https://support.google.com/business/answer/18888417).
*   **Events:** Promote an event at your business.
    *   Add a title, start and end dates, and times. If you don’t provide a start or end time, the event shows as lasting 24 hours on the event dates. You can also include a description, photo, video, and an action button.

**Tip:** Posts older than 6 months are archived unless a date range is set.

## Create a post

1.  [Go to your Business Profile](https://business.google.com/).
2.  Select **Posts** ![and then](//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36) **Add post**.
3.  Select the post type:
    *   **Update**
    *   **Offer**
    *   **Event**
4.  Select the elements you want to add to your post.
    *   To add more details, select the available options, like ![Add](//lh3.googleusercontent.com/tUEOtBsO80Wjgbt43TeB3NH5KyoM30O5Md0WrgJ7T69NpTJxgDoBcI7d1s65SvZo6Fg=h36)Button or ![Add](//lh3.googleusercontent.com/tUEOtBsO80Wjgbt43TeB3NH5KyoM30O5Md0WrgJ7T69NpTJxgDoBcI7d1s65SvZo6Fg=h36)Coupon code.
5.  Add info for your post.
    *   If you want to schedule your post to publish at a later time, turn on **Schedule this post**, then select the date and time you want the post to publish.
    *   If you want to publish your post on a recurring basis, from the “Repeats” dropdown menu, select how often you want your post to show up, such as weekly, monthly, or a custom schedule.
6.  When you’re ready to publish, at the bottom right, select **Post**.
    *   To post across multiple Business Profiles, select the profiles where you want to share it, then select **Post**.
    *   To share the post on one profile, select **Skip**.

**Tip:** To improve your posts, you can add details like a descriptive title, start and end date, and other relevant info. If details change, you can always edit a post to keep info up-to-date.

## Edit or delete a post

You can edit or delete a post after you publish it.

1.  [Go to your Business Profile](https://business.google.com/).
2.  Select **Posts**.
3.  At the right of the post you want to edit or delete:
    *   To edit a post, select More ![](//lh3.googleusercontent.com/iEsZGhIiEJCsmv43PCHdRcC7zUaM4qrDkKcTnMLzYw_rUm7mmzl2bR7nQqDrtjGb4I6T=h36) ![and then](//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36) **Edit**.
    *   To delete a post, select More ![](//lh3.googleusercontent.com/iEsZGhIiEJCsmv43PCHdRcC7zUaM4qrDkKcTnMLzYw_rUm7mmzl2bR7nQqDrtjGb4I6T=h36) ![and then](//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36) **Delete**.

## Understand your post status

After you publish your post, Google reviews it to make sure it [meets our posts content policy](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7213077). Your post’s visibility to customers depends on its status:

*   **Live:** The post is public and shows on Search and Maps.
*   **Pending:** The post doesn't show on Search or Maps. It’s either in the upload stage, the processing stage, or your profile is unverified.
*   **Not approved:** The post doesn't show on Search or Maps. The question mark next to the status indicates which content policy the post violates.

## Tips to improve your posts

*   **Keep it professional:** Avoid misspelled words, extra character
